transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah. I guess I came in because my eating has been getting kind of out of hand, especially after work. I work late shifts, and by the time I’m done I’m tired and wired at the same time, and I’ll stop somewhere for food on the way home—like a full takeout meal, not just a snack—and then when I get back to my apartment I don’t really stop there.

I’ll keep eating whatever’s around, like chips, sweets, leftovers, just… whatever I can find. And in the moment it’s like I’m just going through it, not really thinking clearly, but afterward I look at the containers or wrappers and I’m honestly shocked by how much I ate. It’s embarrassing to say out loud, but that’s the main reason I’m here.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate for what you’ve eaten?

Yeah… um, I do, sometimes. Not every single time, but there have been times after I get home and I’ve eaten way too much—like takeout and then snacks on top of it—where I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up.

It’s hard to say because I know how bad it sounds, and I don’t really talk about it. But in my head, when I’m that full, I start panicking that it’s just going to sit in me and turn into weight, and I feel like I need to get it out. I hate admitting that, but yes, I have done that.
During these times when you're eating a lot, do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating or stop yourself once you start?

Yeah… that’s probably the scariest part, honestly. Once I start on those nights, it doesn’t feel like a normal decision anymore, like, “I’m hungry, I’ll have this and then stop.” It’s more like I’m watching myself from the outside almost, and part of me is saying, “Put it away, close the container, go to bed, you don’t even want this anymore,” but my hands just keep going.

I’ll open one thing, then another thing, and then I’m checking the cabinets or the fridge like I’m on autopilot. Even if I feel uncomfortable or I know I’m going to feel awful after, I keep eating until there’s nothing easy left or until everything I bought is gone. It’s not like I’m enjoying every bite by that point. I feel kind of trapped in it, like I can’t interrupt it once it gets going.
On average, how often do these episodes of binge eating happen—like how many times a week or month?

Um… I’d say most weeks it happens at least once. It kind of became more regular after I moved into my apartment and things settled into a routine, if that makes sense. Like once the move wasn’t taking up all my time and I was just doing the late shifts, coming home tired, being by myself… that’s when it started feeling like there was a pattern.

So, yeah, usually at least one late-night episode in a week where I eat way past what I meant to. And then afterward I’ll panic and try to make up for it somehow—sometimes by making myself throw up, or sometimes I’ll skip breakfast the next morning, or I’ll force myself to go on a really long run even if I’m exhausted. It’s not usually every night, but it’s often enough that I can’t really pretend it’s just a random bad night anymore.
Have these episodes of eating and the things you do afterward affected your daily life, like your mood, relationships, or ability to focus on work or other activities?

Yeah… it has. I mean, I’m still getting to work, so from the outside it probably looks like I’m functioning. I show up for my shifts, I do what I’m supposed to do, I’m not calling out or anything like that. But it’s definitely changed how I’m living around work.

Like after a late shift, if people say, “Let’s go grab food,” I’ve started making excuses. I’ll say I’m tired, or I have something to do early, or I already ate, even if that’s not really the reason. It’s not that I don’t like them—I do—but I get anxious about being around food after work, or about what might happen when I get home if I’ve already eaten with them. So I just avoid it, and then I feel kind of isolated, because I’m the one pulling back.

And the mornings after are… not normal mornings, I guess. Instead of sleeping in a little, or doing laundry, errands, normal adult stuff, I’m thinking about how to make up for the night before. Like my whole morning gets planned around undoing it somehow, rather than actually resting or taking care of what I need to do. It puts me in a bad headspace, and then I’m distracted and kind of ashamed, even if I still manage to get through the day.

Outside of avoiding social situations involving food and the mornings being difficult, have these episodes caused any other problems in your life, like trouble sleeping, feeling depressed or anxious, or issues at work that you hadn’t mentioned yet?

I don’t know that I can point to anything else clearly, if that makes sense. Like, I don’t want to say, “Yes, it’s causing this whole separate problem,” because I’m not totally sure what’s from the eating stuff and what’s just regular stress or being tired from work and late shifts.

Sleep-wise, I mean, some nights I’m up later than I should be, but I don’t know if I’d call it a separate sleep problem. And with work, I’m still going in and doing my job. I don’t think anyone there would say I’m messing things up or anything. I might be in my head sometimes, but I’m not getting written up or missing shifts.

Mood and anxiety… I guess I feel bad about it, obviously, and embarrassed, but I already kind of mentioned that. I’m not sure if there’s something beyond that that I’m not noticing. It’s more like it hangs over me than like there’s been some obvious new crisis, if that makes sense.
Do you feel distressed about your body shape or weight, or has your eating behavior been driven by a fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?

Yeah… yes. I mean, I don’t love saying that, because it sounds kind of vain or ridiculous when I say it out loud, but yes, a lot of it is tied to that.

Even when people at the venue tell me I look too lean, or they’ll make some comment like, “You’re disappearing,” I don’t really take that in the way they probably mean it. It doesn’t reassure me for very long. If anything, I’ll nod or joke it off, but then later if my pants feel even a little tighter, or if I step on the scale and it’s up like one pound, I get this panicky feeling, like it’s immediately visible. Like everyone—guests, coworkers, whoever—is going to notice right away and think I’ve let myself go.

And I know logically one pound or one pair of pants fitting weird probably doesn’t mean anything. Like maybe they shrank in the wash or I ate something salty or whatever. But in the moment it doesn’t feel logical. It feels like, “Okay, this is the start of losing control,” and then I’m really uncomfortable in my own body. So yeah, fear of gaining weight is definitely a big part of what drives it.
Do you ever have episodes of binge eating at times other than during the night after work, like during the day or in the morning?

It’s mostly after late shifts, honestly. That’s the pattern I came in worried about. Like I’ll leave work already feeling kind of keyed up and tired, and I’ll stop for food on the way home—usually something that’s already a full meal, like takeout—and then once I’m home it doesn’t just stop there. I’ll keep going with whatever’s around, like chips, sweets, leftover stuff in the apartment, just kind of moving from one thing to the next.

And then afterward I’ll look at the containers or wrappers or just think back over it and feel shocked, like, “How did that turn into all of that?” It’s not usually a morning thing for me. During the day I might think about food or worry about what I ate, but the really large amounts, the ones where I feel kind of stunned by it afterward, are mainly that late-night-after-work situation.
